Client evaluation and office expansion and AI ad diagnostics discussion

  

## **Client campaign performance and launch strategy**

  - Gillian Conley reported that HiddenGemproperty is testing a 2-week trial with another competing marketing agency.
  - The crowdfunding launch model requires pre-selling reservations 1 year in advance at steep discounts.
  - Traditional financing outperforms crowdfunding by allowing full-price sales and responsive pricing adjustments.
  - Crowdfunding serves as an effective strategy exclusively for validating micro-resort offers and consumer demand.

  

## **Office expansion and amenities**

  - Gillian Conley outlined expanding office square footage into the adjacent garage space for team growth.
  - Makenna Moran proposed converting the second garage bay into an on-site company gym with weights.
  - Gillian Conley suggested installing a smoothie bar stocked with frozen fruit to support employee wellness.

  

## **Meta ads reporting cadence and AI tools**

  - Dustin Baker established a monthly ad budgeting cadence alongside a mid-month creative refresh cycle.
  - Weekly metric monitoring systems identify performance anomalies and out-of-KPI metrics outside standard reporting cycles.
  - HiddenGem AI connected to Claude analyzes performance drops and generates straightforward budget and creative adjustments.
  - Visual diagrams generated via Claude help clients clearly understand ad deconstruction and workflow structures.

  

## **Seasonal content and winter asset strategy**

  - Transitioning northern clients to winter content serves as a best practice for seasonal campaign alignment.
  - Seasonal content updates apply exclusively to northern properties experiencing measurable winter weather conditions.
  - Content intake workflows incorporate specific location-based snow criteria for accurate AI asset generation.

  

## **Next steps**

  - \[Dustin Baker\] Meet with Lan: Discuss the creation of a copy-paste prompt versus system-integrated prompts for ad reporting analysis.
  - \[The group\] Update calendar: Schedule the new monthly ad reporting cadence to ensure consistent performance monitoring.
  - \[Dustin Baker\] Share diagram: Distribute the diagram illustrating the ad deconstruction and analysis process to the team.
  - \[Shawal\] Monitor ad metrics: Review ad KPIs every week to flag performance discrepancies and potential issues.
  - \[Account managers\] Consult managers: Verify creative or budget changes with Shal and Dustin before implementation.
  - \[The group\] Implement winter content: Add winter content to the pipeline for all Tier 01 clients if not already present.
  - \[The group\] Switch seasonal ads: Pause summer advertisement campaigns for northern clients and transition to winter assets.
  - \[Dustin Baker\] Test winter ads: Execute A/B tests in select advertisement accounts to compare summer and winter campaign performance.
  - \[Gillian Conley\] Update intake process: Define location-specific snow requirements in the content intake process for Artificial Intelligence generation.
  - \[Dustin Baker\] Create regional map: Display an office map categorizing client regions by winter weather characteristics.

### **Summary**

**Client Departure Evaluation**  
Client departure highlighted launch boom campaign limitations. Traditional financing remains preferable.  
  
**Office Expansion Plans**

**Meta Ads Management**

### **Decisions**

## **Aligned**

  - **Office space expansion and gym setup** The team agreed to take on extra square footage to create a large hangout area and a company gym in the garage bays.
  - **Monthly cadence for ad performance reviews** The team established a monthly cadence consisting of end-of-month budget reviews and mid-month creative refreshes.
  - **Approval workflow for ad adjustments** Account managers will initially coordinate ad budget and creative adjustments with Shawal and Dustin before gaining full autonomy.
  - **Winter content transition for northern clients** The team established a best practice to turn off summer ad creatives and switch to winter content for northern clients.

  
  

### **Next steps**

  - \[Dustin Baker\] Meet with Lan: Discuss the creation of a copy-paste prompt versus system-integrated prompts for ad reporting analysis.
  - \[The group\] Update calendar: Schedule the new monthly ad reporting cadence to ensure consistent performance monitoring.
  - \[Dustin Baker\] Share diagram: Distribute the diagram illustrating the ad deconstruction and analysis process to the team.
  - \[Shawal\] Monitor ad metrics: Review ad KPIs every week to flag performance discrepancies and potential issues.
  - \[Account managers\] Consult managers: Verify creative or budget changes with Shal and Dustin before implementation.
  - \[The group\] Implement winter content: Add winter content to the pipeline for all Tier 01 clients if not already present.
  - \[The group\] Switch seasonal ads: Pause summer advertisement campaigns for northern clients and transition to winter assets.
  - \[Dustin Baker\] Test winter ads: Execute A/B tests in select advertisement accounts to compare summer and winter campaign performance.
  - \[Gillian Conley\] Update intake process: Define location-specific snow requirements in the content intake process for Artificial Intelligence generation.
  - \[Dustin Baker\] Create regional map: Display an office map categorizing client regions by winter weather characteristics.

  
  

### **Details**

  - **Client Departure and Launch Boom Evaluation**: Gillian Conley discussed a client ending their contract after a crowdfunding-style launch boom campaign did not meet expectations, noting that while the client appreciated the team's work and Alicia's efforts specifically, they are trying a two-week trial with another company ([00:00:14](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.e2wlh5505h3j)). Gillian Conley analyzed that other agencies rely heavily on image ads with overlaid copy, but their cost per result is worse, suggesting the change will not solve the client's core issues ([00:02:47](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.2lcdeg6fx2sh)). Gillian Conley reflected that launch boom strategies often act like "fool's gold," promising millions in pre-sales while forcing developers to slash rates in half before knowing true demand, concluding that traditional financing through private investors is preferable ([00:03:44](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.nqzci7mq58mj)) ([00:05:27](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.44ujam9nvmow)). Gillian Conley noted that the primary benefit of the launch boom model is offer validation, running ads for around $50 to gauge consumer interest in a concept like a cave house or treehouse before building ([00:04:39](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.lj74br2fs030)) ([00:06:27](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.pyy018yb97ai)).
  - **Office Expansion and Gym Plans**: Gillian Conley and Makenna Moran discussed an agreement where an adjacent office wants to downsize, allowing the team to take over the extra square footage by putting up a dividing wall near the fridge, which provides needed expansion room for up to five new team members. Makenna Moran and Gillian Conley outlined plans for the first garage bay to serve as a lounge area with couches and lunch tables, while the second garage bay will be converted into an on-site office gym featuring a bench and weights to promote health, energy levels, and mental clarity ([00:09:07](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.w7f25fyz23w9)). Gillian Conley and Makenna Moran also proposed setting up a smoothie bar in the office equipped with a freezer and fridge stocked with chopped bananas, spinach, and strawberries ([00:11:04](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.qm9sxwuyb4si)).
  - **Meta Ads Categorization and Cadence**: Gillian Conley outlined a tiered system for managing Meta ads, where advanced campaigns involve active budget scaling and creative optimization, while basic campaigns run with simple targeting and minimal adjustments ([00:13:58](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.djco35hl86w)). Gillian Conley and Makenna Moran established a fixed monthly reporting cadence, scheduling budget reviews and scaling decisions at the beginning of the month (e.g., days 1, 2, 5, 6, 7) and creative refreshes in the middle of the month (around the 15th) to monitor frequency, click-through rates, and ad fatigue ([00:14:49](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.gf2hcb67af9i)). Dustin Baker added that weekly automated metric tracking handled by Shawal Nazir will flag anomalies outside of key performance indicators—such as top-funnel costs per lead or drops in return on ad spend—allowing the team to intervene between the scheduled monthly reviews ([00:16:54](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.vx37ucv3qrrb)).

  - **Utilizing HiddenGem AI for Ad Diagnostics**: Dustin Baker explained that when ad performance drops trigger an alert (such as Tabberg Falls' lookalike campaign return on ad spend falling to 3.3x), the team uses the HiddenGem AI tool powered by Claude to diagnose the root cause and generate actionable levers, such as adjusting budgets or refreshing ad creatives. Dustin Baker demonstrated that the AI cross-references property management system data and meta ad performance against internal strategy doctrines to determine if drops stem from seasonality, pacing, or creative fatigue ([00:19:44](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.2muc7f53bwqr)) ([00:23:13](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.mndwc38i0ssa)). Makenna Moran and Dustin Baker discussed formatting AI outputs to maintain flexibility for follow-up questions, client summarization, or visual diagram generation ([00:26:16](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.praj8lo7hi4)) ([00:31:18](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.a8uulkw2zb86)).

  - **AI Visualizations and Content Generation**: Dustin Baker shared that Claude can be used to generate visual diagrams and timelines (such as deconstructing the scenes and hooks of a reel) to clearly articulate marketing value and strategies to clients ([00:32:16](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.s4p4az7l9l65)). Gillian Conley noted that prompt design systems can be fed into Claude to maintain visual and stylistic consistency across client accounts ([00:34:24](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.pugskit63h7m)). Makenna Moran and Chiara Henry discussed blending real influencer content with AI-generated interior and hook clips, emphasizing the need to match lighting and time of day to avoid jarring visual switches ([00:48:24](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.fecogu1yfjp1)).
  - **Account Manager Action Protocols and Testing**: Gillian Conley clarified that account managers should initially coordinate budget or creative changes with Shawal Nazir and Dustin Baker before acting autonomously as they grow more comfortable with the AI tool's recommendations ([00:43:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.cvcvppvk5tw1)). Dustin Baker noted that testing AI-suggested interventions—such as reducing a lookalike campaign budget by 20% rather than pausing it entirely—helps navigate slow seasons without disrupting better-performing retargeting ads ([00:37:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.6nk0sawfagmz)). Makenna Moran asked about operational workflows, confirming that account managers can ask the AI interface directly for interface walkthroughs or hook-rate metric presets ([00:39:40](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.uojeqt7qok7j)).
  - **Seasonal Content Transition to Winter Messaging**: Gillian Conley reported that querying the HiddenGem AI across multiple accounts indicated it is time to transition toward winter or cozy-season messaging and content over October ([00:45:36](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.64yp2vnztex)). Dustin Baker and Chiara Henry debated whether to completely pause summer content or run winter ads alongside summer ones, with Dustin Baker establishing a best practice to turn off summer content in northern regions where winter is visually prominent ([00:46:32](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.2ghdsivrepxk)) ([00:50:32](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.5qoblbmzut0r)). Makenna Moran, Ananya Arora, and Dustin Baker clarified that winter content adjustments apply specifically to northern properties (such as New York) and are unnecessary for desert or southern locations like Walden Retreat in Texas, Arizona, or Joshua Tree where snow does not stick ([00:51:26](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.gm33u4k95c2u)).
  - **AI Image Modification for Winter Weather**: Gillian Conley and Dustin Baker discussed content intake processes for property locations, noting that applying AI winter filters requires calibrating snow depth to match local geography, ranging from a light frost or dusting on the ground for evergreen cabins to heavy roof piles ([00:53:09](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.4pj1nvehkuo7)). Dustin Baker expressed a preference for adding subtle, captivating falling snowflakes or fall leaves to content when it can be executed realistically with cinematic finishing ([00:54:08](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11gWAmc-R6mCIXj3AlG7j_zLyW583SHloC0JPxJCNud0/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.q3kcz4h1275s)).
